solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Profitable, better set of TV adverts?

parts.note: a profitable venture is a commercial one
to better a record is to break it

explanation.surface: A business boasts of being profitable and improving on rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here: you break a record when you better it.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval in a television programme filled with advertisements is called by this name; the question mark admits the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Viscount cavorting with colleen — stand and watch, maybe

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nobleman dances about with an Irish girl while others stand watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' shuffles VISCOUNT and COLLEEN together. A stand of trees and a watch of nightingales are group names, so 'stand' and 'watch' are examples, not verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Group terms like a stand of trees or a watch of nightingales are words naming a gathering, the grammatical category for such terms.

clue.text: Char reportedly fails to register shock

indicators.note: reportedly means the clue words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to fail to register something is to miss it, so misses; a shock of hair is a mop

explanation.surface: Someone is too stunned to take in a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a charwoman, a cleaner; Mrs Mopp was the cleaning lady in the 1940s British radio comedy ITMA, and 'Mrs' is said 'misses'.
explanation.definitionFit: A char is a cleaning woman, and the radio character's name became a byword for any domestic cleaner.

clue.text: Former US tech company worker is in high spirits

parts.note: ex- means former
Uber is the American ride-hailing technology firm
a worker ant, the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An ex-employee of a Silicon Valley firm is cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in high spirits is lively and full of joy, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Sceptic in Cyprus, mostly good- natured

parts.note: CY is the international abbreviation for Cyprus

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word for good-natured is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a good-natured person is nice

explanation.surface: A doubter in Cyprus is, for the most part, kindly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic doubts people's motives, the same as one who distrusts sincerity.

clue.text: Book by Lawrence, or Dr No as a novel?

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new and different, so the letters of the preceding words are made new

explanation.surface: Is this D H Lawrence book, or the Bond story Dr No, a novel?
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun about books but is the anagram signal on OR DR NO AS, with the final A set beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: D H Lawrence published a 1922 novel under this biblical title, about a flautist leaving his family.

clue.text: Easily concealed in Selby farmhouse

indicators.note: concealed in says the letters lie unseen within the following words

explanation.surface: Something is easily kept out of sight in a Yorkshire farmhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Selby is a town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning easily is winning by a wide margin, so the phrase means comfortably or decidedly.

clue.text: Sent a message from upset titled lady touring the Spanish island

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, the whole built word read from bottom to top
touring means going round, so the title wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a dame is a woman holding a title
el is Spanish for the
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A distressed noblewoman on holiday sends word from a Spanish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts ELI inside DAME, giving DELIAME; 'upset' turns that over.
explanation.definitionFit: Messaging someone electronically is sending them a message, the past tense matching 'Sent'.

clue.text: See folk chatting playing game

indicators.note: playing here means fooling about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look at people talking while playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks tied to 'game' but rearranges SEE FOLK CHATTING.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's playground game in which one child holds a mound and others try to push them off.

clue.text: Left one's black ashes vase in a place in Northern Ireland

parts.note: one's read as I'S, the letter I for one plus 'S
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an urn is a vase for a cremated person's ashes

explanation.surface: Someone left their black funeral urn in an Ulster town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisburn is a city just south-west of Belfast, so it is one location in Ulster.

clue.text: Do without chorus

definitions.meaning: to abstain or hold back from doing something
a repeated section of a song

explanation.surface: Manage without the backing singers.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abstain; as a noun it is the burden repeated after each verse.

clue.text: Call up the day before about fair

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for the day before surrounds the word for fair

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival
fair, as in middling, is OK

explanation.surface: Phoning someone the day before a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up a memory or image is to summon it to mind, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Check mostly involves key singer

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the shortened word holds the key
mostly means the restraining word loses its final letter

parts.note: to check is to control or restrain
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A test mainly concerns the pitch a vocalist uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest female voice, and by extension the woman who sings it, is a vocal part name.

clue.text: Ant & Dec upset with rap artist

indicators.note: upset means knocked into disorder, so the letters of the names and the music style are scrambled

explanation.surface: The TV double act are cross with a hip-hop performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant & Dec are a long-running British TV presenting duo; their names plus RAP are the letters mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Artist is used broadly for any performer, so a hoofer in metal-tipped shoes qualifies.

clue.text: NCO imprisoning trainee, ultimately getting physical

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the officer's rank encloses a letter

parts.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned officer

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of trainee

explanation.surface: A non-commissioned officer locks up a recruit and things get rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily, having a material form, as physical does.

clue.text: One going into debt changing part of bathroom suite?

indicators.note: going into means the numeral is put inside the rearranged letters
changing means the letters of debt are altered in order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone running up debt by renovating their bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A low basin for washing is one fixture of a bathroom set, alongside toilet and basin.

clue.text: Start to belly dance in musical

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of belly is used

parts.note: the rigadoon is a lively old French dance for couples

explanation.surface: A belly dancer's first move in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigadoon is the 1947 Lerner and Loewe stage show about a Scottish village that appears once a century.

clue.text: Clear chamber

definitions.meaning: to jump over something, as a pole-vaulter clears the bar
an arched room, often underground, such as a strongroom or crypt

explanation.surface: Empty the room.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means leap over; as a noun it is a secure room or burial chamber.

clue.text: Improve ranking after winning

indicators.note: after means the ranking word comes behind the winning word

parts.note: a team that is winning is up
a grade is a rank or level

explanation.surface: A side moves up the table after a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something to a better standard or level is to make it better, a verb like the definition.

clue.text: Impolite about mine, men in comic opera

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for impolite goes round the rest

parts.note: impolite means rude
a dig is an excavation, a mine
OR, other ranks, is the military term for enlisted men

explanation.surface: Rude remarks about mining folk in a light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an 1887 Gilbert and Sullivan work, one of their light satirical stage pieces.

clue.text: Round and plump and pompous

parts.note: O is round in shape
rotund means plump

explanation.surface: A description of a fat, self-important figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An orotund style is grandiloquent and inflated, which is how a self-important speaker sounds.

clue.text: Garment worn in bed — elasticated thing, good to have

indicators.note: elasticated means stretched out of shape, so the letters of thing are rearranged

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A stretchy bit of nightwear is a good thing to own.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose dress-like garment is nightwear, put on for sleeping.

clue.text: Jewelled headpiece, first-rate, shown in painting put up

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the built word is read from bottom to top
shown in means placed inside the word for painting

parts.note: painting is a form of art
A1 means first-rate, the 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A splendid tiara appears in a portrait hung on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, such as a coronet.

clue.text: Small cuts — nothing by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the slang word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Minor wounds are nothing to worry about, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a tiny notch or cut, so the plural matches small cuts.

clue.text: Member holding head of one with a distinctive smell

indicators.note: holding means the limb encloses the next letter

parts.note: an arm is a member, a limb

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of one

explanation.surface: A club member hugs a leader who has a peculiar odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic scent, pleasant or not, such as that of coffee, is this word.

clue.text: Not informed, a female in Paris defending a battle

indicators.note: defending means surrounding protectively, so the French word goes round the rest

parts.note: une is the French feminine for a
a war is a battle on a large scale

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman, ignorant of events, fights in a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not told about something is ignorant of it, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Odd quote after extremely clever game

indicators.note: after means the jumbled word follows the outer letters
extremely means the two extreme letters, first and last, of clever
odd means strange, so the letters of quote are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peculiar remark follows something very witty.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn sport played by knocking balls through hoops with mallets is this pastime.

clue.text: Statement, perhaps made to tourists in Campania, denies esplanade needs rebuilding

definitions.text: Statement, perhaps made to tourists in Campania

indicators.note: needs rebuilding means the letters must be put together afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Someone denies that the seafront promenade needs repairing.
explanation.walkthrough: Campania is the region of southern Italy whose capital is Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb urges visitors to view the Italian city's beauty before dying, so it is a saying offered to visitors there.
